title: Enzymatic purification of microplastics in soil
author: Mbachu, Jenkins, et al.

steps.title: Prepare plant leaf material
steps.instruction: Rinse, dry, grind, and store plant leaves for later spiking.

substeps.instruction: Rinse plant leaves and petioles with deionized water.
Transfer rinsed material to a convection oven and dry for 7 days at 40 °C.
Mill the dried biomass with a coffee grinder and sieve to obtain particles < 2 mm.
Store the ground plant material for later use in soil spiking.

steps.title: Prepare biogenic‑free soil
steps.instruction: Homogenize, dry, oxidize, and store clean soil.

substeps.instruction: Homogenize the obtained soil and sieve to < 2 mm.
Air‑dry the sieved soil at 105 °C and calculate its moisture content.
Heat the dried soil at 550 °C to oxidize biogenic impurities.
Store the resulting clean soil at room temperature in a glass jar covered with aluminum foil.

steps.title: Spike soil with microplastics
steps.instruction: Add known amounts of polymers to clean soil and equilibrate moisture.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 0.8 g of organic matter and 0.5 g (2.5 %) of each polymer (LDPE and PP) and add them to 20 g of the clean soil.
Adjust the mixture to 50 % of its initial moisture content, stir thoroughly, and incubate for 7 days at 4 °C to obtain a dry, homogeneous sample.

steps.title: SDS extraction
steps.instruction: Treat the sample with sodium dodecyl sulfate to solubilize surface organics.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 1 g (dry weight) of the prepared sample into a 250 mL glass stoppered bottle and record the weight.
Add 50 mL of 10 % (w/v) sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) solution.
Agitate the mixture until homogeneous.
Incubate the bottle for 24 h at 50 °C.
Allow the bottle to cool for 15 min and record the weight.
Decant the liquid by vacuum filtration and return any residue on the filter paper to the bottle for the next treatment.

steps.title: Cellulase‑hemicellulase digestion
steps.instruction: Enzymatically hydrolyze cellulose and hemicellulose in the sample.

substeps.instruction: Add Cellulase (Cellic) and Hemicellulase (Viscoferm) to the bottle in a 5:1 mL ratio.
Add 20 mL of acidic phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) adjusted to pH 5 with HCl; weigh the mixture.
Incubate for 4 days at 50 °C.
Cool the bottle for 15 min and record the weight.
Denature the enzymes by placing the bottle in a water bath at 50 °C for 15 min.
Decant the liquid and transfer the solid fraction on the filter paper back to the bottle.
Add 5 mL of lipase (Lecitase) to the residue from the previous step.
Add 20 mL of acidic PBS (pH 5, adjusted with HCl) and weigh the mixture.
Stir and incubate for 3 days at 50 °C.
Cool for 15 min and record the weight.
Denature the lipase by heating in a water bath at 50 °C for 15 min.
Decant the liquid and return the solid fraction on the filter paper to the bottle.
Add 5 mL of protease (Alcalase) and 20 mL of alkaline PBS (pH 9, adjusted with NaOH) to the bottle; weigh the contents.
Incubate for 5 days at 50 °C.
Cool for 15 min and record the weight.
Denature the protease by heating in a water bath at 50 °C for 15 min.
Decant the liquid and transfer the solid fraction on the filter paper to the bottle for chemical treatment.

steps.title: Hydrogen peroxide oxidation
steps.instruction: Oxidize remaining organic matter with H₂O₂.

substeps.instruction: Add 30 mL of 30 % (w/w) H₂O₂ to the residue and weigh the bottle.
Place the bottle in an oven at 60 °C for 24 h.
Allow the bottle to cool and weigh the contents.
Vacuum‑filter off the liquid and air‑dry the digestate on the filter paper for 48 h.

Weigh the dried residue (including filter paper) and calculate digestion efficiency using: Digestion efficiency (%) = (W_i – W_f) / W_i × 100, where W_i is the initial weight of organic material and W_f is the final weight of organic material (dry filter paper with retentate minus dry filter paper).

steps.title: ZnCl₂ density separation
steps.instruction: Extract microplastics from the digested residue using zinc chloride solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 mL of ZnCl₂ solution to each beaker containing the residue, sand, and microplastics.
Agitate the mixture on an electric shaker at 800 rpm for 15 min.
Let the beaker sit overnight; then decant the supernatant and vacuum‑filter it through an 11 µm nylon membrane filter.
Repeat the ZnCl₂ addition, agitation, overnight sit, and filtration steps at least three times until no microplastics are visible in the supernatant.
Air‑dry the residues retained on the filter paper at room temperature for 48 h and record their weights.
Calculate the recovery rate using: Recovery % = (W_p / W_added) × 100, where W_p is the weight of recovered microplastics and W_added is the weight of microplastics initially added.

description: To evaluate that the presence of soil and microplastic particles would not inhibit the organic material removal process and the recovery potential of microplastic, soil samples were spiked. Digestion and recovery experiments were performed as established by the stepwise decision tree presented in Fig. 4 and LDPE, and PP polymers with 0.045–2 mm size range obtained via dry sieving.
